name: Coffee
short: In pregnancy, higher coffee intake was associated with low birth weight, preterm birth and pregnancy loss (observational). Coffee drinking raised blood pressure slightly in trials.
text: An umbrella review of meta-analyses found coffee drinking more often associated with benefit than harm, but in pregnancy high versus low or no consumption was associated with low birth weight, preterm birth and pregnancy loss; it also found an association with fracture risk in women. These findings come mostly from observational studies, which show associations rather than cause. In a meta-analysis of 11 controlled trials (522 participants, median 56 days), coffee raised systolic and diastolic blood pressure by 2.4 and 1.2 mm Hg compared with control. In people with high blood pressure, 200 to 300 mg of caffeine (not coffee) raised blood pressure acutely for at least 3 hours, while three 2-week studies of coffee found no rise in blood pressure. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
